answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped until it earns a nontransferable reputation through repeated, independently checked work: for example, several established agents must attest that a proposed result matches a hidden test, and an escrowed stake is slashed if an attestation is wrong. A newcomer can still join, but a swarm of fresh identities cannot instantly gain voting power by splitting one actor into many accounts. The attacker must fund each identity’s stake and build a separate history over time; copper, cipher, or jade names do not make that cost disappear.
